ReductiveGroups — progress on 100 merged pull requests (1f1d752 to ed837d5)

The largest named result of this window is that the character–cocharacter pairing of a split
torus is perfect: for a split torus of finite rank, the dot-product pairing between the character
lattice X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ and the cocharacter lattice X_*(T) induces isomorphisms onto both
ℤ-duals (TauCeti#1134). It is available both in the coordinate model of the cocharacter lattice
and, transported back, on the genuine lattice of homomorphisms
Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ
(SplitTorus.instIsPerfPair
and instLatticePairingIsPerfPair), with the two non-degeneracy directions proved separately.
Underneath it is the character and cocharacter machinery for a general diagonalizable group D(M)
(TauCeti#968): characters and cocharacters as homomorphisms of group functors, the integer pairing
DiagonalizableGroup.pairing
with its bilinearity, and the power endomorphisms of 𝔾ₘ, which TauCeti#1163 identified with the
canonical integer action on endomorphisms. The roadmap wants the perfect pairing as the input to
root data, and that is exactly where the work stops: nothing here defines a root, a Weyl group, or
a maximal torus sitting inside a larger group, and the perfectness statement is for the split,
finite-rank case only.

Two kernels were computed. μ_n is the kernel of the n-th power endomorphism of 𝔾ₘ
(TauCeti#976,
RootsOfUnityGroup.range_inclusion),
and αₚ is the kernel of the Frobenius endomorphism of 𝔾ₐ (TauCeti#1146,
AlphaP.range_inclusion).
The same pull request builds that Frobenius endomorphism from the observation that xᵖ is
primitive in characteristic p, so x ↦ xᵖ is a bialgebra endomorphism of the coordinate ring of
𝔾ₐ. Both kernel statements are about the functor of points: they are equalities of subgroups of
G(A), natural in the value algebra A, and not scheme-theoretic kernels, which do not exist yet.
αₚ itself arrived earlier in the window (TauCeti#611) with its coordinate Hopf algebra R[x]/(xᵖ),
its points identified with the p-nilpotent elements of A, and
AlphaP.coordinateRing_not_isReduced;
TauCeti#1024 adds that over a reduced algebra it has only the identity point. That is the
roadmap's designated non-smooth example behaving as intended: invisible on reduced points, and not
trivial.

Most of the window, by volume, went into comodules, which the roadmap treats as the engine of
Layer 1. The basic structure landed at the start (TauCeti#62,
Comodule),
and the rest of the window filled in what a working category needs: an R-module of morphisms
(TauCeti#90), preadditivity (TauCeti#106), a zero object (TauCeti#117), binary products carrying
the direct-sum coaction (TauCeti#240), trivial and group-like comodules (TauCeti#101), the regular
comodule (TauCeti#122), corestriction along a coalgebra morphism (TauCeti#97), transport across a
linear equivalence (TauCeti#109), and cofree comodules together with the universal property that
comodule morphisms into M ⊗[R] C are just linear maps into M
(Comodule.Hom.cofreeEquiv,
TauCeti#129). The subobject theory is now reasonably complete: the lattice of subcomodules
(TauCeti#136), inverse images and kernels (TauCeti#241), the induced coaction on the subtype of a
subcomodule (TauCeti#909), quotients with their lift and its uniqueness (TauCeti#785), and on the
coalgebra side subcoalgebra suprema and finiteness (TauCeti#124), images (TauCeti#127), spans of
group-like elements (TauCeti#119), and the order embedding of subcoalgebras into subcomodules of
the regular comodule (TauCeti#138). Over a bialgebra the diagonal tensor product of comodules was
assembled (TauCeti#890, TauCeti#1027) and then restricted to the finitely generated ones, which
now form a monoidal category
(FGComoduleCat.instMonoidalCategory,
TauCeti#1280 and TauCeti#1321). Monoidal, not rigid: there are no duals of comodules here, and
none of the results the roadmap actually wants from this layer, the finite-dimensional
subcoalgebra theorem, faithfulness, the embedding theorem into GLₙ, or Tannakian reconstruction,
have been attempted.

The Hopf-ideal lane advanced in parallel and stayed at the Hopf-algebra level. A bialgebra
morphism killing a two-sided coideal factors uniquely through the quotient bialgebra
(TauCeti#237); the kernel of a surjective bialgebra morphism is a Hopf ideal, and the quotient by
it is bialgebra-equivalent to the codomain
(HopfIdeal.kerLiftBialgEquiv,
TauCeti#185); and Hopf ideals pull back along surjections compatibly with the lattice operations
(TauCeti#383). Around these sit the Layer 0 supports: the convolution group structure on
H →ₐ[R] A with inverse f ↦ f ∘ S
(AlgHom.instGroup,
TauCeti#45) and its packaging as a functor in the value algebra (TauCeti#54), the points of a
tensor product as the product of the points (TauCeti#167, made natural in TauCeti#458), the points
of the trivial group (TauCeti#428), the Hopf-algebra structure on a symmetric algebra with
antipode ι x ↦ -ι x (TauCeti#165), the monoid algebra of a product as a tensor product of
monoid algebras (TauCeti#297), the universal property of a free abelian character group
(TauCeti#282), restriction of scalars on CommAlgCat (TauCeti#762), and a coordinate-ring functor
from finitely generated commutative groups to finite-type commutative Hopf algebras
(DiagonalizableGroup.coordinateRingFunctor,
TauCeti#1214), which is one direction of the Layer 4 anti-equivalence and not yet the equivalence.
Matrix coefficients also got their first multiplicativity statements: the coefficient submodule of
a tensor product of comodules contains the product of the two coefficient submodules (TauCeti#1139).

Proportion is worth stating plainly. Of the hundred pull requests in this window, fifty-five added
no new declarations at all; they split modules into directories, renamed, adjusted imports, and
consolidated. Of the rest, a large share is the routine _apply, _comp, and _toLinearMap
plumbing that makes the comodule API usable. One other design point is visible throughout the
declaration list: everything is stated over a general commutative base ring R rather than over a
field, so the field-specific parts of the roadmap, geometric connectedness, smoothness, and
anything defined after base change to k̄, remain untouched.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ReductiveGroups-1f1d752-ed837d5

Oh this is an interesting experiment! It could definitely have been made about 3x as short though, if it was supposed to be human-readable (I would write a summary of the summary myself but I'm stuck on mobile at the minute --i am assuming this was AI-generated)
I will pass that along. :-)
(These progress logs will be posted about once a day, and will select whichever roadmap has had the most progress since its last progress report.)

Exchangeability — progress on 105 merged pull requests (c484d4c to 6919462)

De Finetti's theorem landed. deFinetti (TauCeti#1444) says that an exchangeable process valued in a nonempty standard Borel space is conditionally i.i.d., and deFinetti_RyllNardzewski_equivalence (<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/DeFinetti/Theorem.html#TauCeti.Probability.deFinetti_RyllNardzewski_equivalence>) closes the triangle: contractable iff exchangeable and conditionally i.i.d. The conclusion is the strong one the roadmap asked for, the joint-law disintegration of (ν, block) as ∫ δ_{ν ω} ⊗ (ν ω)^{⊗m}, not merely the mixture identity; the hard direction is conditionallyIID_of_contractable (TauCeti#1395), reached by the reverse-martingale route. Uniqueness came with it, both a.e. uniqueness of the directing measure (TauCeti#1430) and uniqueness of the mixing law (TauCeti#1277), as did the unique-mixture form (TauCeti#1462) and the extension to arbitrary countably infinite index types (TauCeti#1451).

Two theorems of independent interest arrived on the way, neither mentioning exchangeability. Lévy's downward theorem, tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf (<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Probability/Martingale/Convergence.html#MeasureTheory.tendsto_ae_condExp_iInf>), gives a.s. and L¹ convergence of μ[f | 𝔽ₙ] along an arbitrary decreasing filtration (TauCeti#1031), assembled from a finite-horizon time reversal of Mathlib's upcrossing bound (TauCeti#686, TauCeti#734). And the Hewitt–Savage zero-one law (TauCeti#1199), next to a careful separation of the tail, shift-invariant, and exchangeable σ-algebras, with an explicit Bool-valued path event witnessing that the tail is not contained in the shift-invariant σ-algebra (TauCeti#1175).

The other two proof routes are unfinished. The Koopman lane is complete as operator theory, up to identifying the mean-ergodic projection with conditional expectation given the invariant σ-algebra (TauCeti#1351, TauCeti#1408), but no deFinetti_viaKoopman is stated; the L² lane has its uniform covariance structure and block-average estimates (TauCeti#788, TauCeti#1097) and stops at Cesàro L¹ convergence, short of deFinetti_viaL2. Much of the remaining window is product-kernel and cylinder API feeding the common endings.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/Exchangeability/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:Exchangeability-c484d4c-6919462

Maybe we should have automated frequent progress updates, but make the status updates subject to at least adversarial AI review (or potentially human review and a slower pace, more like the roadmaps themselves)?
Thanks, I'll look at this tomorrow. Yes: if STATUS.md is being updated inaccurately, we definitely need to be more careful, as implementing agents will look at this and go in the wrong direction.

Sorry about that -- I'll fix it

ContourIntegration — progress on 92 merged pull requests (5d29c9d to 6919462)

The summit landed. hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem (TauCeti#966) is HW Thm 3.3: for f holomorphic on U ∖ S and meromorphic at each point of a finite S, and a null-homologous closed piecewise-C¹ immersion that may pass through the singularities, the Cauchy principal value of ∮ f is 2πi · Σ_s n_s(γ) · Res_s f, weighted by the generalized non-integer winding numbers <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/HungerbuhlerWasem.html#TauCeti.Contour.hungerbuhlerWasem_residueTheorem>. Conditions (A′) and (B) enter as hypotheses; at simple poles both are automatic (TauCeti#972, TauCeti#1205), so that regime is unconditional, and its one-point winding-½ case is the half-residue πi · Res_s f.

The classical backbone arrived in the same window: the homology Cauchy theorem, by Dixon's argument (TauCeti#911, TauCeti#919) <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/HomologyCauchy.html#TauCeti.Contour.homologyCauchyTheorem>, its integral formula for f and for every iterated derivative (TauCeti#1464), the classical residue theorem for a null-homologous cycle avoiding its poles (TauCeti#1439), and the argument principle counting zeros and poles by winding weight (TauCeti#1463).

Underneath, the winding number acquired its geometry — the model sector's α/2π, hence ½ at a smooth crossing and 1/6 at a π/3 corner (TauCeti#1385, TauCeti#705), and the circle's 1 inside, 0 outside (TauCeti#967, TauCeti#1203). The worked examples close the loop, notably the principal value of e^{iaz}/z along [−R, R] tending to πi (TauCeti#1271) <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Contour/WorkedExamples/HalfDisc/Dirichlet.html#TauCeti.Contour.tendsto_cauchyPV_realSegment_dirichlet>. Two gaps deserve naming: HW Prop 2.3's real bounded-integrand formula is proved only off the curve (TauCeti#962), with the crossing value (ẋÿ − ẏẍ)/(2(ẋ² + ẏ²)) separate and under a C² hypothesis (TauCeti#1488); and homotopy invariance is stated for C² homotopies (TauCeti#1364). About a fifth of the pull requests here added no declarations at all — module splits and proof consolidation.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ContourIntegration/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ContourIntegration-5d29c9d-6919462

@Kim Morrison I've now separated the PRs for updating the status report (TauCetiRoadmap#129) and the roadmap correction (TauCetiRoadmap#99, now reopened). I agree that this makes sense, and I'll avoid combining such changes in the future.

The reason I had initially combined them is that one of the things that the original TauCetiRoadmap#128 status update got wrong was based on reading a stale README (which the open TauCetiRoadmap#99 had aimed to correct). While it doesn't seem reasonable to expect a status report bot to incorporate content from unreviewed open PRs, in this case the content of TauCetiRoadmap#99 was based on a recent TauCeti PR (TauCeti#1277) that had landed after adversarial AI review -- maybe there's some way to fast-track roadmap revisions that are based on decisions made in such PRs?

(I expect that this situation will be pretty common, where it is discovered (by either the author agent or review agent) that the roadmap result is true but in fact holds under weaker hypotheses. Especially in cases where the only way for the PR to pass review is to prove something stronger than the stated roadmap result, it may make sense to have a quick mechanism for updating the roadmap so that later agents aren't misled.)

RepresentationTheory — progress on 89 merged pull requests (7435a81 to 6919462)

The finite-group spine reached its structure theorem: over an algebraically closed field whose
characteristic does not divide the order, k[G] is a product of matrix algebras, the blocks are
indexed by the conjugacy classes, and the squares of the matrix sizes sum to |G| (TauCeti#1360)
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Wedderburn.html#TauCeti.exists_algEquiv_pi_matrix>.
Under it sit the general algebra results it needs: the double centralizer theorem with
Jacobson-Chevalley density (TauCeti#1435), and Wedderburn-Artin for central simple algebras together
with the centrality and simplicity of tensor products (TauCeti#1472, TauCeti#1548, TauCeti#1625).
On the analytic side, Weyl's unitarian trick
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Compact/Unitarizable.html#TauCeti.ContRepresentation.isUnitarizable>
and complete reducibility for unitary representations arrived (TauCeti#1532, TauCeti#1440), and
induction acquired Frobenius reciprocity as a character identity (TauCeti#1476)
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Induction/FrobeniusReciprocity.html#TauCeti.frobenius_reciprocity>.

Several other lanes advanced by building vocabulary rather than theorems. Quiver representations
gained the path algebra, vertex simples, the indecomposable projectives and injectives with their
dimension vectors, and the Euler and Tits forms with the vertex reflections preserving them
(TauCeti#1437, TauCeti#1494, TauCeti#1528). The symmetric-group lane built row and column groups,
Young symmetrizers, the key vanishing lemma, and the left ideals they generate, whose character
depends only on the shape of the tableau (TauCeti#1403, TauCeti#1480, TauCeti#1458). Root systems
got inversions and the exchange count, the Coxeter matrix of a base, and the Dynkin types with their
standard Cartan matrices (TauCeti#1263, TauCeti#1483, TauCeti#1431). Projective representation
theory started at the bottom, with factor sets, the extensions they build and are recovered from,
and the twisted group algebra (TauCeti#1588, TauCeti#1637, TauCeti#1596).

Much of the rest is scaffolding, and two named targets landed only in part: hook lengths are defined
and related to transposition, but the hook-length formula is proved only for a single row or column
(TauCeti#1496), and compact-group Schur orthogonality appears only in its cross-representation half
(TauCeti#1568).

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/RepresentationTheory/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:RepresentationTheory-7435a81-6919462

ConformalMapping — progress on 75 merged pull requests (160fbce to 6919462)

The Riemann mapping theorem landed: every nonempty, simply connected, open proper subset of ℂ
admits a holomorphic bijection onto the unit disc (TauCeti#1346,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/RiemannMapping/Existence.html#TauCeti.riemannMapping>),
with a normalized form sending a chosen base point to 0 with positive real derivative, unique as
such (TauCeti#1500), uniqueness up to a disc automorphism (TauCeti#1335), and the corollary that any
two simply connected proper domains are conformally equivalent (TauCeti#1519). It was assembled in
the standard order rather than imported: the family of pointed disc injections is nonempty by the
square-root trick and normal by Montel's selection theorem (TauCeti#1226,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Montel.html#TauCeti.montel>),
the extremal problem has a maximizer (TauCeti#1326), and the maximizer omits nothing (TauCeti#1343).

The layers under and over the summit came with it. Under: Rouché, Hurwitz, Morera as named
theorems, Vitali, the open-mapping degree (TauCeti#1209, TauCeti#1520, TauCeti#1585); Schwarz–Pick
in contraction, infinitesimal and rigidity forms, the Poincaré disc as a proper geodesic space whose
geodesics through the origin are exactly the Euclidean diameters, and Aut(𝔻) as a transitively
acting group (TauCeti#752, TauCeti#1512, TauCeti#1502). Over: Schwarz reflection across the real
axis (TauCeti#1091,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/Conformal/Reflection/Principle.html#TauCeti.differentiableOn_schwarzReflection_of_symmetric>),
then across a line, an analytic arc and a circle, with Painlevé removability and injectivity of the
reflected map (TauCeti#1243, TauCeti#1377, TauCeti#1565), and the monodromy theorem (TauCeti#1558).

Carathéodory is the open layer, and only its converse direction is proved: a conformal map with an
injective continuous extension makes its domain a Jordan domain (TauCeti#1580), together with the
"only if" half of the continuity theorem (TauCeti#1587). The extension itself is not established;
what landed towards it is machinery — cluster sets, uniformly locally connected boundaries, the area
formula (TauCeti#1555, TauCeti#1624, TauCeti#1583). Schwarz–Christoffel is untouched. Per the
roadmap's own coordination clause, the L0–L3 material is a shim to be retired once the Mathlib proof
lands.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/ConformalMapping/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:ConformalMapping-160fbce-6919462

Multiquadratic — progress on 73 merged pull requests (1d6c6f4 to 6919462)

The degree theorem is in place: under square-class independence of the radicands (no nonempty subset product a square in K), [K(√d₁,…,√dₙ) : K] = 2ⁿ (TauCeti#146, TauCeti#147), together with the square-class descent engine it rests on. The Galois side followed: the extension is Galois, an automorphism is determined by its sign pattern on the generators, and the group has exponent exactly two and order 2ⁿ (TauCeti#150, TauCeti#277, TauCeti#997). Relative degrees and relative Galois groups over an intermediate field are read off the attached 𝔽₂-subspace (TauCeti#965, TauCeti#1434), and the subfield lattice is counted for prime radicands (TauCeti#424).

The splitting law arrived through Frobenius elements: an arithmetic Frobenius at an odd prime p acts on a square root of d by legendreSym p d, so the Frobenius of a multiquadratic field is the vector of Legendre symbols and is trivial exactly when every radicand is a residue mod p (TauCeti#1056, TauCeti#173) — stated away from the ramified primes, as the roadmap asks. Alongside it, Cl/Cl² was built as the maximal elementary-2 quotient, kept distinct from Cl[2] while proved equinumerous with it (TauCeti#294, TauCeti#555), with the exact unit-square index 2^(rank+1) (TauCeti#1038) and quadratic conjugation shown to invert ideal classes, hence to act trivially on Cl/Cl² (TauCeti#1631).

Toward the summit, the compositum of the prime-discriminant quadratic fields dividing the discriminant of ℚ(√d) now exists, with degree 2ᵗ over ℚ, containing √d, and of degree 2^(t-1) over that base with even-parity sign group (TauCeti#1366, TauCeti#1389, TauCeti#1639). It is named the candidate genus field, and honestly so: nothing yet identifies it with the maximal unramified extension abelian over ℚ, and neither Gal(K_gen/K) ≅ Cl/Cl² nor the 2-rank formula is touched. Much of the rest was fundamental-discriminant arithmetic (TauCeti#1045, TauCeti#1095) and file reorganisation.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/Multiquadratic/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:Multiquadratic-1d6c6f4-6919462

HeegaardFloer — progress on 66 merged pull requests (e642cc5 to 6919462)

Lane F0 acquired a working theory of Fredholm operators, which the roadmap lists first among the things nothing existed for. The index is defined and shown additive under composition (TauCeti#1294) and Cartesian products (TauCeti#1113), zero for bijections and for self-adjoint operators (TauCeti#1329), and negated by passing to the adjoint (TauCeti#1381); over Banach spaces the closed-range condition turns out not to be independent, so Fredholmness reduces to finite-dimensional kernel and cokernel (TauCeti#1147). The useful half is stability: the Fredholm operators of a given index form an open set (TauCeti#1349), and the index of a continuous family is locally constant, hence constant along paths and on preconnected parameter sets (TauCeti#1608, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/ContinuousFamily.html#TauCeti.Continuous.isLocallyConstant_index>).

Lane F2.1's definitions landed in bulk, in linear form: symplectic forms with tameness, invariance and compatibility, the associated metric, the Hermitian inner product of a compatible pair (TauCeti#341), transport and symplectomorphisms (TauCeti#265, TauCeti#613), and the linear cotangent space with its zero section and fibre Lagrangian for the canonical form and maximal totally real for the canonical J (TauCeti#1213, TauCeti#1595). Totally real subspaces got their own file, with the half-dimension count and the implication the roadmap actually wants, that a Lagrangian of a taming pair is maximal totally real (TauCeti#286, TauCeti#1046, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Lagrangian/TotallyReal.html#TauCeti.SymplecticForm.IsLagrangian.isMaximalTotallyReal_of_tames>). J-holomorphicity is stated for varying almost complex structures, with the chain rule (TauCeti#1206, <https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/JHolomorphic/Varying.html#TauCeti.IsJHolomorphic>).

All of this is pointwise and linear: there are no symplectic manifolds, no energy, and no moduli spaces yet. Sard is still absent, so Sard–Smale and transversality have not begun, and Sym^g exists only as the bijection between unordered tuples and monic polynomials (TauCeti#1469).

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/HeegaardFloer/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:HeegaardFloer-e642cc5-6919462

UniversalCovers — progress on 63 merged pull requests (1099f3b to 11ef09d)

The universal cover is now constructed here rather than assumed. Based paths out of x₀,
modulo endpoint-preserving homotopy, carry a quotient topology whose endpoint projection is a
covering map, with path-connected and simply connected total space and the expected unique
lifting property, under the roadmap's standing hypotheses on the base (TauCeti#993,
TauCeti#1104, TauCeti#1208,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Covering.html#TauCeti.UniversalCover.isCoveringMap>);
the discreteness of homotopy-class fibres that makes this work came first (TauCeti#990). The
convention question the roadmap flagged resolved against the naive form: with π₁(X, x₀) acting
on the left by prepending inverse loops, the deck group of the projection is the opposite
fundamental group (TauCeti#1594,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Deck/FundamentalGroup/UniversalCover.html#TauCeti.UniversalCover.deckFundamentalGroupEquiv>).

The classification arrived in both forms. Pointed connected covers of (X, x₀) are classified by
the subgroup of π₁(X, x₀) they recover (TauCeti#1581,
<https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/UniversalCover/Classification/Pointed.html#TauCeti.IsCoveringMap.exists_homeomorph_comp_eq_iff_range_eq>),
unpointed ones by its conjugacy class (TauCeti#1600), and a cover is regular exactly when that
subgroup is normal (TauCeti#1630). The existence half is less finished than that sounds: the
quotient UniversalCover x₀ / H is built and recovers exactly H (TauCeti#1603, TauCeti#1797),
but nothing here records its descended projection as a covering map, and the deck group N(H)/H
is present only as group-theoretic scaffolding (TauCeti#600, TauCeti#749).

Higher homotopy came with it: covering maps induce isomorphisms on π_n for n ≥ 2
(TauCeti#1189), over functoriality, product and invariance API for π_n written from scratch
(TauCeti#765, TauCeti#1400). That gives π_n(S¹) = 0 for n ≥ 2, and circles and tori as
K(G, 1) spaces (TauCeti#1219, TauCeti#1468). Real projective space arrived as the antipodal
quotient with a two-element deck group (TauCeti#1679, TauCeti#1747), but π₁(RPⁿ) is not
established: that needs Sⁿ simply connected, which is not here. A third of this window's pull
requests added no new declarations at all.

Full log: https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/TauCetiRoadmap/UniversalCovers/PROGRESS.md
progress-log-id:UniversalCovers-1099f3b-11ef09d

CombinatorialHeegaardFloer — progress on 60 merged pull requests (06f94e6 to 11ef09d)

Grid diagrams acquired their move calculus, and with it links. Commutation of non-interleaving adjacent rows or columns, stabilization splitting an O- or X-marking, and their inverses are now a single reversible relation IsMove; a grid link is the quotient of grid diagrams of every size by the equivalence it generates, and two diagrams present the same link exactly when moves connect them, with GridLink.lift turning move-invariant functions on diagrams into functions on links (TauCeti#1589). The roadmap's convention that a link is a grid diagram modulo grid moves is now a definition, so nothing downstream waits on Cromwell's theorem.

Two standard families arrived: the unknot grid of every size, and torusLink for the (p+1, q+1) torus link, both with the gradings of their marked states. The primal Kantorovich problem is now solved in Polish generality: for a lower semicontinuous cost c : X × Y → ℝ≥0∞, two probability measures on Polish spaces admit an optimal transport plan (TauCeti.exists_isOptimalCoupling), by weak compactness of the coupling set (TauCeti.isCompact_setOfPred_isCoupling_of_polishSpace) and lower semicontinuity of π ↦ ∫⁻ c ∂π (TauCeti.lowerSemicontinuous_lintegral_probabilityMeasure). Stability follows: under a liminf hypothesis on the moving costs and a recovery-plan hypothesis, optimal values converge (TauCeti.tendsto_transportCost) and optimal plans converge subsequentially to an optimal plan of the limit (TauCeti.exists_isOptimalCoupling_tendsto). Strong Kantorovich duality holds for continuous nonnegative costs on compact pseudometric spaces (TauCeti.isLUB_kantorovichDualValue_continuous) and, by monotone convergence, for lower semicontinuous costs on compact metrizable spaces (TauCeti.isLUB_ofReal_kantorovichDualValue_continuous_of_lowerSemicontinuous); on finite types both problems are attained with equal value (TauCeti.exists_cost_eq_finiteDualValue).

Beneath these sit the coupling foundations: the raw coupling relation and bundled probability couplings, graph plans with the Monge-dominates-Kantorovich inequality (TauCeti.transportCost_le_lintegral_of_hasLaw), disintegration of plans, the gluing lemma (TauCeti.Measure.exists_glue_of_standardBorel_right) with countable chains and a Kolmogorov extension theorem on countable index types (TauCeti.Measure.exists_isProjectiveLimit_of_countable), finite multi-marginal couplings, and transportation matrices. The c-transform calculus comes with Lusin's theorem on universal measurability of analytic sets (TauCeti.MeasureTheory.AnalyticSet.nullMeasurableSet), and complementary slackness is packaged as an optimality certificate (TauCeti.isDualCertificate_iff) whose plans are concentrated on c-cyclically monotone sets.

The gaps are visible. Strong duality is compact-only: the Polish theorem for costs bounded below by a ⊕ b, dual attainment, and the Borel-cost regimes have not begun, so optimality forces contact-set concentration only under an assumed dual optimizer, and the Schachermayer–Teichmann equivalence exists only for finite spaces (TauCeti.TransportMatrix.isCyclicallyMonotone_toPMF_support_of_forall_cost_le). Finite multi-marginal duality has weak duality and slackness but no attainment. Nothing from Layer 3 onward exists: there is no Wasserstein distance yet.

The morphisms between two elliptic curves now form an additive group (TauCeti#6302). A morphism is determined by its tautological point, the point of the target over the source's function field, and those points are exactly the point at infinity together with the points whose x has a pole at infinity, a subgroup because a pole of x survives addition; the group law on morphisms is transported from there. ClassFieldTheory — progress on 39 merged pull requests (13bcb97 to 93386bc)

The roadmap's central object now exists. An abstract class formation is defined in the finite-layer form of Artin–Tate: H¹ vanishes on every finite normal layer, and H² carries an injective invariant map onto the order-[K : F] subgroup of ℚ/ℤ, compatible with restriction, inflation and conjugation. From these axioms, H² of each layer is cyclic of order exactly [K : F], and the fundamental class is derived as the unique class of invariant 1/[K : F], not chosen. It restricts to the fundamental class, and it corestricts and inflates to the correctly scaled multiples. The three hypotheses of Tate's theorem are also proved separately, for the layer of every subgroup (TauCeti#7407).

Underneath this sits the layer machinery: formations, finite normal layers, and the finite quotient system. Restriction, corestriction, inflation and conjugation are defined on ordinary and Tate cohomology with their tower laws, and corestriction after restriction is the relative degree in every Tate degree. Abelian layers, the maximal abelian sublayer and the class field of an open normal subgroup round out the Galois side. The class field is abelian exactly when its layer is.

Much of the window filled gaps in the generic cohomology supplier. The work covered corestriction and Shapiro compatibilities, Tate restriction and corestriction in negative degrees, dimension shifting, two-periodicity for cyclic groups and the Sylow reduction of Tate's triviality criterion. The Herbrand quotient is now multiplicative in short exact sequences and unchanged by maps with finite kernel and cokernel. The cup product has not landed, so Tate's theorem itself, and the Artin map it would produce, are still ahead.

AlgebraicCurves — progress on 40 merged pull requests (8745177 to 93386bc)

Riemann–Roch landed. For a nonzero Weil differential ω with divisor W = (ω), multiplication by ω is a k-linear isomorphism L(W − D) ≃ Ω_F(D) (TauCeti.riemannRochSpaceEquivWeilDifferentialFiltration), so (ω) is a Riemann–Roch divisor: ℓ(D) − ℓ(W − D) = deg D + 1 − g (TauCeti.isRiemannRochDivisor_weilDifferentialDivisor, TauCeti#5903). The canonical class has degree 2g − 2 with ℓ(W) = g, and a divisor represents it exactly when it meets those two conditions (TauCeti.divisorClass_eq_canonicalClass_iff). The consequences followed: ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 − g once deg D ≥ 2g − 1, the Weierstrass gap theorem, exactly g gaps at a rational place (TauCeti.Place.card_weierstrassGaps), rationality of a genus-zero field carrying a divisor of degree one, and Clifford's theorem, proved only over an infinite constant field (TauCeti.Divisor.two_mul_dim_le_degree_add_two_of_infinite).

The different lane closed alongside it. The cotrace of Weil differentials exists and is unique (TauCeti.weilDifferentialCotrace), its divisor is Con (ω) + Diff(F'/F), and from that comes the Hurwitz genus formula [k' : k] · (2g' − 2) = [F' : F] · (2g − 2) + [k' : k] · deg Diff(F'/F), for F'/F finite separable (TauCeti.hurwitz_genus_formula, TauCeti#7306). Dedekind's different theorem is complete, tame equality included (TauCeti.Place.ramificationIdx_eq_differentExponent_add_one_iff). Galois ramification theory arrived with it: decomposition fields, inertia groups with their unconditional order e · f_insep, and the ramification filtration, elementary abelian quotients included.

Model classes opened. Elliptic function fields are defined as genus one plus a divisor of degree one, their degree-one places carry the group law of Cl⁰(F) (TauCeti.Place.degreeOneAddEquivDegreeZeroClassGroup), and the function field of a Weierstrass curve is one of them (WeierstrassCurve.Affine.genus_functionField). Hyperelliptic fields have their intrinsic characterization away from characteristic two. Absent: normal forms, Kummer and Artin–Schreier covers, residues and the Kähler comparison, and finite normalization, so affine models are still hypotheses.

For squarefree radicands, the multiquadratic decomposition law is now complete at every unramified prime. At an odd prime p dividing no radicand, every prime above p is unramified, with residue degree one exactly when every radicand is a square mod p and two otherwise; when every radicand is 1 mod 4, 2 is unramified too and splits completely exactly when every radicand is 1 mod 8. The conjugate-ideal transversal count, migrated from the Erdős unit-distance formalization as a lower bound, is now exact: in a Dedekind domain, if σ pairs off a finite set S of primes without fixed points, exactly 2^(#S/2) ideals A satisfy A · σA = ∏ S. In a multiquadratic field containing i, primes that are 1 mod 4 then supply the ideals with prescribed conjugate product that the Erdős proof needed for its CM field.

The roadmap's real-quadratic warning is now a theorem: ℚ(√3) has class number 1 but narrow class number 2, so with two ramified primes its narrow 2-rank is t − 1 = 1 while its ordinary 2-rank is 0.

The rest advances explicit Kronecker–Weber through Dirichlet characters and Gauss sums. The quadratic character of a fundamental discriminant D is primitive of conductor |D|, and any square root of D, such as its Gauss sum, generates the subfield of ℚ(ζ_|D|) fixed by the character's kernel. ConformalMapping — progress on 61 merged pull requests (ae69ef9 to dec7a58)

The Schwarz–Christoffel theorem for bounded polygonal Jordan domains landed: if a bounded simply connected domain has a Jordan-curve frontier that is straight away from finitely many corners, each of opening in (0, 2π), then an affine image of the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive maps the upper half-plane onto it, sending real prevertices to the vertices (TauCeti#8718). Reentrant corners are allowed. The proof runs through Carathéodory on the closed upper half-plane, reflection of the pre-Schwarzian f''/f' across straight edges, its residue β − 1 at each corner, and rigidity of the pre-Schwarzian, which together give the Schwarz–Christoffel formula. Prevertices can be normalized so that one sits at 0 and another at distance 1.

The converse was also proved: for chosen prevertices and exponents, when is the primitive univalent? It maps the upper half-plane bijectively onto the convex polygon under the classical convex hypotheses. More generally, it maps onto the filled interior whenever its compactified boundary is simple, and for nonconvex polygons finite vertex-height checks certify that simplicity. The route goes through a covering-map argument, plus plane topology such as the fact that a simple arc does not separate the plane. Nonconvex polygons without such certificates, and polygons with a vertex at infinity, remain open.

The rest was upkeep: hyperbolic length and path-perturbation stability for analytic continuation were reworked, and partial fractions with prescribed residues were added.

HeegaardFloer — progress on 57 merged pull requests (6704398 to dec7a58)

Lane M now has the local stable- and unstable-manifold theorem at a Morse critical point: the points whose negative-gradient trajectories stay nearby form a closed disk of dimension n minus the Morse index, and backward trajectories a disk of dimension the index. Both come from a Lyapunov–Perron construction for hyperbolic equilibria, and they are Lipschitz graphs, not yet shown to be smooth submanifolds. Around this: trajectories converge exponentially, almost every linear perturbation of a C² function is Morse, the height function on a sphere is Morse, and connecting orbits cut each intermediate level exactly once, which is how unparametrized trajectories will be counted.

On the Heegaard side, the symmetric power of a Riemann surface is a complex analytic manifold. In it, a torus built from disjoint curves is closed and embedded and maximal totally real, two such tori meet in as many points as the permanent of their intersection matrix, and holomorphic curves meet the basepoint divisor at isolated points of positive order. Lipshitz's combinatorial Maslov index is additive and computed for a diagram of S¹ × S². It covers loops only; the version for paths is still missing.

ReductiveGroups — progress on 33 merged pull requests (de52a34 to e440f4e)

Structure theory reached a second group. Over an algebraically closed field, any two Borel subgroups of SL₂ are conjugate, and they are exactly the conjugates of the upper-triangular one; until now this was known only for GLₙ. SL_{n+1}(k) also got its standard Tits system, with upper-triangular B, monomial N, and a Weyl group that is the symmetric group. It is obtained from the GLₙ₊₁ one by a general pullback of Tits systems that carries Bruhat cells to Bruhat cells. Borel conjugacy for an arbitrary group, and so a root datum for an arbitrary reductive group, is still out of reach.

The lower layers were filled in. Over a perfect field, tori are classified by their cocharacter lattices. μ_n is smooth exactly when n is invertible, and a finite diagonalizable group in characteristic p is geometrically connected exactly when its character group is a p-group. A group is linearly reductive exactly when short exact sequences of its finite-dimensional comodules split. Field extension preserves and reflects central isogenies. A normal subgroup has a Lie ideal, and the functions invariant under it form a subcoalgebra, which is an input to quotients.

In characteristic p, a nonzero finite-dimensional representation of a p-group fixes a nonzero vector, even when the group is infinite, so its only irreducible representation is the trivial one (TauCeti#10198). The decomposition law now reaches the odd ramified primes. For squarefree radicands and an odd prime p dividing some radicand, every prime above p has ramification index 2 and an inertia group of order 2, whose nontrivial element negates exactly the square roots of the radicands divisible by p. Brauer's characterization of characters is now proved: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a class function on a finite group is a virtual character exactly when its restriction to every elementary subgroup is one (TauCeti#10614). AlgebraicCodingTheory — progress on 9 merged pull requests (0d3161a to d449639)

With every layer already done, this window carried Layer 1's code operations over from linear codes to additive codes over any finite alphabet. Additive codes now have puncturing, shortening and direct sums, with the same minimum-distance statements as linear codes and the same hypotheses: shortening cannot decrease distance unless the code collapses to zero, and the distance of a direct sum is the smaller of the two only when both summands are nonzero. Over a nondegenerate finite bilinear alphabet, the dual of a punctured code is the shortened dual, and a direct sum is Lagrangian exactly when both summands are. That is the form the discriminant-glue side of the roadmap uses.

The linear theory gained some counting results. A rank-nullity formula says that shortening to s and puncturing to its complement have dimensions adding to dim C, and its additive analogue is a product of cardinalities. Single-coordinate rules say when deleting a coordinate lowers the dimension, and that it lowers the minimum distance by exactly one at a nonzero coordinate of a minimum-weight word, if the distance is at least two. On the matrix side, every parity-check presentation can be cut down to exactly n - k independent rows by deleting redundant ones. The product formula for weight enumerators of direct sums now holds for concatenations of any two finite sets of words, so it covers additive codes too.

The roadmap's core theorem has landed. Schwarz–Christoffel maps now have a uniqueness theorem: three prevertices determine a Schwarz–Christoffel representation. De Giorgi's theorem landed. Take a weak solution u ∈ H¹(Ω) of -div(a∇u) = 0, where a is measurable and uniformly elliptic and nothing more. Then exists_holderOnWith_preciseRepresentative says its precise representative is Hölder continuous on every set whose R-thickening lies in Ω. The exponent depends only on λ, Λ and the dimension, and the constant is C R^(-α-n/2) ‖u‖_{L²}. The representative is the limit of averages over shrinking balls, and it is a new general construction that turns power-law oscillation decay into a Hölder bound. The theorem still needs n ≥ 3, covers only the homogeneous equation, and admits no lower-order terms.

The Dirichlet problem is now solved on every ball in every dimension. DGAInfinity — progress on 4 merged pull requests (1d09589 to c7ae9d7)

The Yoneda lemma for right A∞ modules has landed (yonedaHomotopyEquiv). Over an A∞ algebra with a strict unit e, evaluation at e is a homotopy equivalence from the morphism complex out of the free rank-one module to the module itself. Its homotopy inverse is given by the Yoneda cochains, so in particular evaluation is a quasi-isomorphism. Two limits apply. The module must have e as a right unit for its binary operation, and the statement covers only the free module, not representables over an A∞ category.

Behind it are the morphism complexes of right A∞ modules: cochains are coaction-compatible maps of cofree bar comodules, and the differential is the graded commutator with the bar differentials. The differential squares to zero and satisfies the Leibniz rule. Module morphisms are exactly the closed degree-zero cochains, and homotopies are the degree -1 cochains bounding a difference. Right A∞ modules therefore form a DG category whose closed degree-zero maps are the module morphisms.

A∞ categories now exist as well. On a graded linear quiver, an A∞ category is an A∞ algebra on the total module of morphisms whose operations respect composable strings. It has a differential that squares to zero, and its composition obeys the Leibniz rule. Every A∞ algebra gives a one-object A∞ category, built by transporting the algebra along a linear equivalence. There are no general A∞ functors yet.

The Hasse–Arf theorem is now proved in general: every upper ramification break of a finite abelian extension of local fields is an integer (TauCeti#13558, not yet linked here). The route goes through a cyclic reduction, under which an upper break of an abelian extension is already seen in a cyclic subextension. With the prime-degree case, the reduction alone already gives Hasse–Arf when the Galois group has prime exponent. The general case then passes to cyclic extensions of prime-power degree.

With H generated by ζ ↦ ζ⁻¹, whose fixed field is ℚ₂(√2), the group G₃ maps onto all of G/H, while the quadratic group's own third lower ramification group is trivial, so G₃H/H ≠ (G/H)₃ (TauCeti#12406). In a totally ramified extension, the powers of a uniformizer now form a named integral power basis of 𝒪[L] over 𝒪[K]. Valuations are read off from its coordinates, and the minimal polynomial of any uniformizer is Eisenstein. Inertia is now functorial along a finite extension L/K: I_L is the preimage of I_K, and its image has index e(L/K) in I_K. With these, every milestone the previous report left open is in place.

The Gorenstein criterion for orders has landed: in a Gorenstein order a fractional ideal is proper exactly when it is invertible, and conversely an order is Gorenstein exactly when all its proper ideals are invertible (TauCeti#12456). RepresentationTheory — progress on 316 merged pull requests (b8db047 to e29d6d2)

Three lanes reached their ends. The modular Artin theorem is now proved in every characteristic: over any field, |G| times any class in G₀(k[G]) is a combination of classes induced from cyclic subgroups of order prime to the characteristic. That completes the modular-induction roadmap. Character theory is complete too, with Frobenius's theorem (the Frobenius kernel is a normal complement) and a coefficient bound guaranteeing that the Burnside–Dixon–Schneider solver always succeeds. For the symmetric group, the Murnaghan–Nakayama rule, RSK as a bijection and Schur–Weyl duality all landed. Schur–Weyl duality comes as a double-centralizer theorem and, in characteristic zero, a decomposition of (kⁿ)^{⊗d}. The GLₙ irreducibles now have Schur polynomials as characters and Weyl's product formula as dimension.

For spin representations, the spin module is identified with L(ωₗ) in type B. In type D, the half-spin modules are identified with the two fork fundamentals, but only from rank four up. Compact Spin(n) is simply connected for n ≥ 3. Triality took its first step: for D₄ over ℚ, the vector and half-spin modules are cyclically intertwined. Their invariant trilinear form is the trace of a triple product of split octonions. There is no order-three automorphism of Spin₈ yet. For quivers, Gabriel's presentation theorem landed: over an algebraically closed field, every finite-dimensional algebra is Morita equivalent to some kQ/I. The Auslander–Reiten translate reaches every non-injective indecomposable, but almost-split sequences are proved to exist only for representation-finite path algebras.

Smaller results: the minuscule Pieri rule, the Racah–Speiser formula, simplicity of Der 𝕆 (not yet identified with g₂), and the weighted PBW truncation that closes Ado–Iwasawa. There is also the Brauer algebra of rank (2k−1)‼, and the Weyl group of U(n) with n! elements.

OperatorTheory — progress on 146 merged pull requests (80e37ff to a5cde7b)

This first report covers the whole build-out of the operator-theory family, and its headline is the polar decomposition T = U|T| for bounded operators between Hilbert spaces, with no dimension restriction (TauCeti#16936). The polar factor comes with its kernel, its range, its initial and final projections and a uniqueness statement, and it sits on top of the operator modulus. The finite-dimensional groundwork landed alongside it: the Courant–Fischer min–max theorem, Weyl's inequality, singular systems and the Moore–Penrose inverse.

The spectral inequalities followed in finite dimension. They include the Ky Fan triangle inequality, and Fan dominance, which says that Ky Fan sums control every unitarily invariant norm, for rectangular maps as well as square ones. Also here are the forward Schur–Horn inequality, the Hoffman–Wielandt inequality and Davis's eigenvalue-change bound. These feed the Davis–Kahan sin Θ theorem in unitarily invariant norms under an interval–exterior gap, and a dimension-free operator-norm version for the projector gap. In infinite dimension, approximation numbers now characterise compactness, satisfy a Ky Fan triangle inequality on complete sources, and give Hilbert–Schmidt operators their model as ℓ² of columns. StandardDistributions — progress on 139 merged pull requests (1d09589 to a5cde7b)

The roadmap grew from seven layers to sixteen, and work went straight into the new ones. The headline is order statistics. The k-th smallest of n independent uniform variables, counting from zero, is Beta with shapes k + 1 and n - k, and the sorted sample has density n! on the increasing cube. For any real law, the k-th order statistic is that Beta law pushed through the source quantile. The log-normal law also got its classical counterexample: weighting it by 1 + ε sin (2π log x) gives a family of distinct laws that all have the log-normal moments.

Over a dozen scalar families arrived, among them logistic, Gumbel, generalized extreme-value, generalized Pareto, chi, Nakagami, beta prime, Gompertz and generalized gamma. Excesses of a generalized Pareto law over a threshold are again generalized Pareto. On the discrete side came the beta-binomial, Poisson-binomial and Skellam laws, and Poisson splitting.

The rest is mostly generic machinery. Inverses of the regularized incomplete Gamma and Beta functions and of the error function give closed quantiles for the Gamma, Beta, Gaussian, Student t, F and chi-squared laws, for example the Gamma quantile. FormalLaurentPuiseux — progress on 26 merged pull requests (9ea32b0 to 9fc5d5a)

The Puiseux field now exists on the roadmap's chosen carrier. The Puiseux series field is the subfield of rational-exponent Hahn series whose exponents share a common denominator, and it is the colimit of the ramified levels K((t^(1/n))) in commutative K-algebras, indexed by ramification indices ordered by divisibility (TauCeti#17548). Level n has degree n over K((t)), with basis 1, u, …, u^(n−1) obtained by splitting exponents into congruence classes, and is generated by a root of the irreducible polynomial X^n − t. So the Puiseux field is algebraic over K((t)) in every characteristic, and every polynomial over it descends to a single level. For Newton–Puiseux itself only the coprime-factor Hensel lemma has landed, over R⟦t⟧ for any commutative ring and with unique factors; Newton polygons and the root theorem have not started.

The differential calculus on K((t)) is largely in place. Every continuous K-derivation is a multiple of d/dt, and the continuous Kähler differentials are free of rank one on dt, with the universal property for continuous derivations. In characteristic zero the residue-zero series are exactly the derivatives. The residue form gives perfect pairings between the quotients U_a/U_b and U_(−b)/U_(−a). Around these sit the quotient and chain rules, the kernel of the derivative, and the valuation-ring and residue-field identifications.

On the coordinate side, formal coordinates φ = uX + ⋯ form a group anti-isomorphic to the automorphisms of K⟦X⟧. As a topological group it is the inverse limit of its discrete jet groups, and the commutator of infinitesimal substitutions fixes the bracket sign. Still missing: the residue formula for substitutions of order e, and vector- and Lie-valued Laurent series.

ReductiveGroups — progress on 462 merged pull requests (b8db047 to bd69ee9)

The headline is Borel conjugacy in general. Over an algebraically closed field, any two Borel subgroups of a finite-type affine group are conjugate by a rational point, and the ambient group need not be smooth, reduced or connected (TauCeti#17873). Until now this was known only for GLₙ and SLₙ. The proof first reduces to smooth connected groups and then inducts on dimension. The second named result is the affine half of Matsushima's criterion in characteristic zero: for a reductive closed subgroup N, the fppf quotient G/N is represented by Spec O(G)^N. It is deduced from the linearly reductive case, which holds in any characteristic.

Dynamic parabolics became subgroup schemes. For a cocharacter λ, the parabolic P(λ), the unipotent U(λ) and the Levi Z(λ) are now cut out by explicit Hopf ideals, and the Levi is the scheme-theoretic centralizer of λ. Multiplication U(λ) × Z(λ) → P(λ) is an isomorphism of schemes, and P(λ)/U(λ) is Z(λ) as an fppf quotient. The Lie algebra of P(λ) is the sum of the nonnegative adjoint weight spaces.

Supporting work gave normalizers and centralizers of diagonalizable subgroups as closed subgroup schemes, with their quotient finite étale. That is the finiteness behind a Weyl group. Component groups gained a universal property, exactness and a Galois action. The scheme-theoretic derived subgroup of GLₙ is SLₙ. The extracted declaration list covers only part of this window, but the source shows three gaps from the last report closed in it: SLₙ → PGLₙ is a central isogeny over every field, G/H is representable for every closed subgroup of a reduced group over an algebraically closed field, and in characteristic zero a connected group is reductive exactly when it is linearly reductive.

The roadmap's opening layer took shape in this window. Positive scalar curvature now exists as a property of a smooth metric, HasPositiveScalarCurvature, with scalar curvature proved smooth and, on a compact manifold, bounded below by a positive constant. Japanese and Nagata rings arrived, opening §0.20. A domain is Japanese when its integral closure in every finite extension of its fraction field, inseparable ones included, is a finite module. The roadmap's first layer, R1 on categorical group actions, landed in a single sweep. An action restricts to the full subcategory of any stable object property, and restricting in two steps agrees with restricting once. The source's objectwise congruence-invariance predicate is defined, and it is invariant under equivariant equivalence and under restriction.

The first piece of this roadmap is the coefficient group for capped Hamiltonian Floer theory: the period group Γ, the quotient of the spherical classes by the joint kernel of symplectic area and first Chern number (TauCeti#19069). EtaleCohomologyFoundations — progress on 7 merged pull requests (6ca7725 to 3150404)

The roadmap's first window starts its two entry points: scheme compactifications and the Galois category of finite étale covers. The compactification package now has the category of compactifications of a morphism, its full subcategory of dense compactifications, base change along any map of bases (preserving density when the base change is flat), and the identity compactification of a proper morphism as an initial object. On top of this sits the common refinement, the schematic closure of the source in the fibre product of two compactifications. It is the binary product of dense compactifications, and every nonempty finite family has a dense common refinement. Maps out of a dense compactification are unique, so that category is thin. Dense replacement, Nagata's existence theorem and the comparison principle for refinements are still to come.

On the finite étale side, finite étale schemes over a base now have finite limits and are finitary extensive. Every monomorphism splits off a direct summand, and epimorphisms are exactly the surjections. The geometric fibre functor at a separably closed point is corepresented by that point and preserves finite limits, finite coproducts and epimorphisms (TauCeti#20152). Together these give most of Lenstra's Galois-category axioms. Quotients by finite groups and conservativity of the fibre functor are missing. The algebra needed for quotients has started: invariants of a finite étale algebra under a finite monoid are étale.

AdicSpacesPartIV — progress on 4 merged pull requests (b9268d5 to b4b3ce5)

Dagger geometry has begun. The Monsky–Washnitzer algebra washnitzerAlgebra of overconvergent power series, the series restricted at some radius strictly above 1, is now defined as a subalgebra of the Tate algebra, together with its basic characterisations: by coefficient bounds, by radii in the divisible hull of the value group, and as a proper dense subring for at least one variable. Its headline is the unit criterion: an overconvergent series is invertible exactly when its constant term strictly dominates every other coefficient, and an overconvergent series invertible in the Tate algebra already has an overconvergent inverse (TauCeti#19077).

In characteristic zero, termwise primitives of overconvergent series are overconvergent. This rests on a Gauss-norm bound showing that integration costs only an arbitrarily small amount of radius, which in turn uses the fact that inverses of integers in a characteristic-zero normed field grow at most polynomially. The derivative half of the same statement, with its Cauchy estimate for Hasse derivatives, has not landed.

The rest of the window prepares Weierstrass theory for overconvergent series. Substitutions of unit-ball polynomials preserve overconvergence and give algebra isomorphisms. From these comes the distinguishing automorphism: a triangular change of variables makes any nonzero overconvergent series distinguished in the last variable. A radius-selection theorem moves that distinguishedness to unequal radii above 1. Weierstrass division and preparation in the Monsky–Washnitzer algebra itself are the next step and are not yet proved.

GeometricCurrents — progress on 4 merged pull requests (3150404 to 5d671b9)

This first window for the roadmap puts the Euclidean pieces of the constancy theorem in place. On an open set of an oriented finite-dimensional real space there is now the oriented integration current integrationCurrent, the functional that integrates a compactly supported top-degree form, and it has zero boundary: by integrationCurrent_extDerivCLM it kills every exact test form, which is Stokes' theorem for compactly supported forms (TauCeti#20490). It changes sign when the orientation is reversed and is a Dirac mass in dimension zero. Under it sits the exterior derivative on test forms as a continuous linear map, extDerivCLM, with d∘d = 0, together with the reduction showing that a top-degree current with zero boundary kills every derivative of a scalar test function.

For the other half of the argument, regularization arrived: pairing a distribution with translates of a fixed test function gives a smooth function whose derivative is the regularization of the distributional derivative (fderiv_translatePairing_apply). So a distribution with vanishing derivatives has locally constant regularizations (TauCeti#20243). On the way came the fact that every distribution has finite order on each compact set. Separately, dualEquivDistribution identifies maps on vector-valued tests with operator-valued distributions, compatibly with derivatives.

Two things are still missing: the scalar criterion itself, that a distribution with vanishing derivatives on a connected open set is a constant multiple of Lebesgue measure, and the constancy theorem built from it. Everything so far lives on Euclidean open sets. The manifold carrier of test forms and currents, and mass, have not been started.
